why: Standard SQL (key words, functions and types of the SQL standard or shared by every major engine): one meaning in both dialects, so both offer it.
The name is in both, but the meaning or the form differs by dialect. Each dialect offers it only in its own form (see each entry).

notes.BEGIN: T-SQL: a block or BEGIN TRANSACTION. PostgreSQL: start a transaction, or open a block in PL/pgSQL.
notes.BINARY: T-SQL: a fixed-length byte type. PostgreSQL: a keyword of the legacy BINARY comparison and type modifiers; the type is bytea.
notes.BIT: T-SQL: the 0/1/NULL type. PostgreSQL: a bit string type.
notes.CLOSE: T-SQL and PostgreSQL both close a cursor, with different surrounding syntax.
notes.CONVERT: T-SQL: CONVERT(type, value [, style]). PostgreSQL: convert(bytes, source_encoding, dest_encoding), a bytea function.
notes.CURSOR: T-SQL: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR .... PostgreSQL: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR ... inside a transaction, WITH HOLD options.
notes.DAY: T-SQL: the function DAY(date). PostgreSQL: a field name for EXTRACT and interval qualifiers.
notes.DEALLOCATE: T-SQL: free a cursor. PostgreSQL: free a prepared statement.
notes.DECLARE: T-SQL: declare variables and cursors anywhere. PostgreSQL: declare a cursor in SQL, or the variable section of PL/pgSQL.
notes.DISABLE: T-SQL: DISABLE TRIGGER / ALTER INDEX ... DISABLE. PostgreSQL: ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER / RULE / ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
notes.ENABLE: T-SQL: ENABLE TRIGGER. PostgreSQL: ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE TRIGGER / RULE / ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
notes.EXECUTE: T-SQL: run a procedure or string (EXEC). PostgreSQL: run a prepared statement.
notes.FETCH: T-SQL: read from a cursor, and OFFSET ... FETCH. PostgreSQL: the same two, with different syntax around them.
notes.FORMAT: T-SQL: FORMAT(value, format [, culture]). PostgreSQL: format(template, args...), a printf-style function.
notes.GLOBAL: T-SQL: a cursor scope. PostgreSQL: the legacy GLOBAL TEMPORARY table spelling.
notes.IDENTITY: T-SQL: the IDENTITY(seed, step) column property. PostgreSQL: GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY.
notes.ISNULL: T-SQL: the function ISNULL(a, b). PostgreSQL: the postfix test `expr ISNULL` (the same as IS NULL); the function does not exist.
notes.LOCAL: T-SQL: a cursor scope. PostgreSQL: SET LOCAL and LOCAL TEMPORARY.
notes.MONTH: T-SQL: the function MONTH(date). PostgreSQL: a field name for EXTRACT and interval qualifiers.
notes.OFF: T-SQL: SET option OFF. PostgreSQL: a boolean value of SET and of a few options.
notes.OPTION: T-SQL: the query-hint clause OPTION (...). PostgreSQL: a word inside OPTIONS (...) of foreign-data objects.
notes.RULE: T-SQL: the deprecated CREATE RULE (a column constraint object). PostgreSQL: CREATE RULE, a query rewrite rule.
notes.SNAPSHOT: T-SQL: the SNAPSHOT isolation level. PostgreSQL: SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT 'id'.
notes.STATISTICS: T-SQL: SET STATISTICS IO/TIME and CREATE STATISTICS. PostgreSQL: CREATE STATISTICS only.
notes.TEXT: T-SQL: the deprecated large-object type. PostgreSQL: the ordinary unlimited string type.
notes.TIMESTAMP: T-SQL: a synonym of rowversion, not a date. PostgreSQL: the date-and-time type.
notes.XMLNAMESPACES: T-SQL: WITH XMLNAMESPACES (...). PostgreSQL: XMLNAMESPACES inside XMLTABLE.
notes.YEAR: T-SQL: the function YEAR(date). PostgreSQL: a field name for EXTRACT and interval qualifiers.
